Running stages as cluster jobs

Source: vignettes/dag-cli.Rmd
dag-cli.Rmd

The xcms and target-list routes can be split into four stages that only communicate through files in a shared tmp_dir. Each stage is one carpediams() call, so a workflow manager (gwf, Snakemake, Nextflow, SLURM arrays) can run the per-sample and per-batch stages in parallel.

prepare ──> sample 1..N ──> filter 1..B ──> finalize ──> MGF

For a step-by-step version in one R session, see vignette("xcms-interactive").

Stages

Stage Runs Reads Writes
prepare once input (and targetlist) manifest.csv, fd.rds; xcms route also mssubset.rds, sample_topfeatures.rds
sample per file files from prepare, the mzML sample_<i>_pool.parquet, sample_<i>_pointers.parquet
filter per batch fd.rds, all sample parquets features_batch_<b>.parquet
finalize once fd.rds, all features_batch_*.parquet the MGF

<i> is sample_idx in manifest.csv. filter splits the features into n_batches contiguous slices and processes slice batch_idx. finalize binds every features_batch_*.parquet it finds. If there are none, it filters all features itself, which makes the filter stage optional for small runs.

Arguments every call needs

  • input: carpediams() uses it to pick the route. Only prepare reads it, so pass the path, not a loaded object.
  • targetlist (target-list route): needed at every stage. Without it, a single mzML input is routed to process_mzml().
  • tmp_dir: the same directory for every stage. If it is left as NULL, a temporary directory is created and deleted when the call returns.
  • output: only needed by finalize.

Keep stage-specific parameters identical across jobs: ppm and rt_buffer (xcms) or ppm and rt_width (target list) for every sample job, and the same grouper, group_statistics_fn and filter_fn for every filter job and for finalize.

The calls (xcms route) 

library(carpeDIAMS)
input   <- "grouped_xcms.rds"
tmp_dir <- "work/carpediams"

# prepare
carpediams(input = input, tmp_dir = tmp_dir, stage = "prepare",
           subsample = TRUE, subset_size = 100, top_n = 10)

# sample, one job per row of manifest.csv
carpediams(input = input, tmp_dir = tmp_dir, stage = "sample",
           sample_idx = 1, ppm = 20, rt_buffer = 5)

# filter, one job per batch
carpediams(input = input, tmp_dir = tmp_dir, stage = "filter",
           batch_idx = 1, n_batches = 200,
           grouper   = pelt_grouper(p0 = 15, Isat = 1e5),
           filter_fn = correlation_filtering(cor_thresh = 0.5, fdr_thresh = 0.01))

# finalize
carpediams(input = input, tmp_dir = tmp_dir, stage = "finalize",
           output = "results/all_features.mgf",
           grouper   = pelt_grouper(p0 = 15, Isat = 1e5),
           filter_fn = correlation_filtering(cor_thresh = 0.5, fdr_thresh = 0.01))

sample_file = "<basename>.mzML" can be used in place of sample_idx.

The target-list route is the same, with targetlist added to every call and rt_width in place of rt_buffer. Its prepare has no subsample or top_n, because every target is extracted from every file.

From the shell

Each call fits in an Rscript -e line, which is all a job template needs:

Rscript -e 'carpeDIAMS::carpediams(input = "grouped_xcms.rds",
  tmp_dir = "work/carpediams", stage = "sample", sample_idx = 17,
  ppm = 20, rt_buffer = 5)'

The number of sample jobs is the number of rows in manifest.csv, which only exists after prepare. Either read it in a second planning phase (Snakemake checkpoint), or declare the jobs up front from a known sample count. n_batches can be any number, because batches past the last feature write an empty parquet.

Memory

  • sample: holds one file’s spectra.
  • filter: DuckDB reads the parquets of all samples for the batch’s features. It is capped at memory_limit = '128GB' and 2 threads, and spills to <tmp_dir>/.duckdb_tmp. Raise n_batches to lower memory per job.
  • finalize with batches: reads the batch parquets, which are small.

Failures and reruns

  • A sample or filter job failed: rerun that job; it overwrites its own files.
  • Changed filter settings: delete features_batch_*.parquet, rerun filter and finalize. The sample parquets are reused.
  • Changed n_batches: delete the old batch files first, because finalize binds every batch file it finds.
  • Changed prepare or sample settings: start from an empty tmp_dir.

Checking that all sample files exist before filtering:

manifest <- read.csv(file.path(tmp_dir, "manifest.csv"))
expected <- c(sprintf("sample_%d_pool.parquet",     manifest$sample_idx),
              sprintf("sample_%d_pointers.parquet", manifest$sample_idx))
setdiff(expected, list.files(tmp_dir))

On the xcms route, a sample with no top-top_n feature writes no files, so a missing pair is not always an error. Look for the sample’s message in the job log.
